page.layout: One printed page: one column of running text; two marginal notes in the left margin, beside the second and fourth paragraphs; running head at top; catchword "Sed" at bottom right.

main_text.p: sufficiens persoluit. Rom. 3. v. 24. 25. 1. Pet. 3. v. 18. Ief. 53. v. 12. Et sic est pro peccatis nostris plena propitiatio, 1. Ioh. 2. v. 2. Hac de re postea fusius.

Satisfecit autem Christus Deo offenso, pro parte offendente, scilicet humano genere, perfectam voluntati divinae obedientiam usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis praestando, & eidem plenae obedientiae dignitatem summam, nimirum Meritum coram Deo & Efficaciam tribuendo. Iohan. 17. v. 19. Act. 20. v. 28. 2. Corinth. 5. Nempe quia Deus erat in Christo Mundum reconcilians sibi, non imputando iis peccataipsorum[?].
Expiatio peccatorumExpiavit itaque Christus peccata nostra Merito passionis & mortis suae, quo persolutis peccatorum poenis satisfecit Iustitiae Dei, Iramque ejus placavit.
Sacrificium expiatoriumVide hic SACRIFICIUM illud (de quo paulo post disceptabitur) quo se Christus Servator offert Deo Patri ad persolvendum poenas peccatis nostris debitas. Heb. 9. v. 26.

page.notes: Printed page number at top left is faint and read as 11; uncertain. Show-through from the reverse side in the left margin is omitted. The word "peccataipsorum" is run together at the line end and may be "peccata ipsorum"; marked [?]. The reference "Ief. 53." is read as printed and may be an abbreviation of Iesaiae. Both left-margin notes are small italic and were read with some difficulty; the wording is as far as legible.
